card.title: SOVIET MILITARY RESEARCH
card.text: Choose One - Add AEROSANI to hand OR EXPANDED SOVIET RESEARCH to hand.
card.flavorText: Soviet military research in WWII often focused on practical answers to urgent battlefield problems. The T-34 illustrated this approach clearly. Its sloped armor did not make the tank invulnerable, but it increased effective protection without adding the weight of much thicker vertical plates. This helped the T-34 combine armor, speed, and a powerful gun in a design that surprised German forces in 1941. This idea was not invented in the Soviet Union, but Soviet engineers used it on a mass-produced tank with exceptional effect. Other wartime projects followed the same practical logic. Katyusha rocket launchers gave the Red Army a cheap and mobile way to deliver sudden heavy fire, able to move before enemy counterfire could respond. Aerosani (propeller-driven sledges) offered reconnaissance, transport, and light raiding ability in deep snow where normal vehicles struggled. Soviet weapons research didn’t stop at armor and artillery. For instance, the 7.62×39mm intermediate cartridge was designed in 1943 for a new family of infantry weapons, including carbines, automatic rifles, and light machine guns.
